ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, the coordinate of point \(A\) is \( \left(2, 3\right) \), the coordinate of point \(B\) is \( \left(4, 0\right) \), and point \(C\) is located in the fourth quadrant. If the quadrilateral formed by the vertices \(O\), \(A\), \(B\), and \(C\) is a rhombus, what are the coordinates of point \(C\)?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Given the property of a diamond that its diagonals are perpendicular and bisect each other, it is known that points $A$ and $C$ are symmetrical about the $x$-axis,\\
since $A(2, 3)$,\\
the symmetry about the $x$-axis keeps the $x$-coordinate the same and changes the sign of the $y$-coordinate,\\
therefore $C(2, -3)$,\\
thus, the answer is: $C=\boxed{(2, -3)}$.
